QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_32

question.text: After novation, how does the Clearing Corporation honour its settlement guarantee if a clearing member defaults on its obligations?

answer.text: It draws on the defaulting member's margins and deposits first, then the Settlement Guarantee Fund and the CC's own resources in a pre-defined default waterfall
It cancels the affected trades and refunds all counterparties at the previous day's closing price
It directs the non-defaulting counterparty to recover the loss directly from the defaulter
It requests SEBI to underwrite the loss before settlement can be completed

explanation.text: The Logic: Because the CC has interposed itself as the central counterparty through novation, it must complete settlement even when a clearing member defaults. The CC follows a pre-defined default waterfall: the defaulting member's initial margin, mark-to-market collections and deposits are used first, then the Settlement Guarantee Fund and the CC's own contributed capital, in that order. The Trap: The CC does not cancel matched trades or revalue them at prior closing prices, non-defaulting counterparties are insulated from chasing the defaulter directly, and SEBI does not underwrite individual settlement losses on demand. Note: Rewritten away from the duplicate novation definition (covered by item _11) to test the settlement-guarantee / default-waterfall concept instead.
